title: How It Works - Orbital Temple
heading: How It Works
intro: The Orbital Temple project consists of three interconnected elements that work together to send names to the temple in space.
paragraph1: The satellite orbits Earth at an altitude of about 500 to 560 km, carrying in its memory the more than 19,000 names sent before launch. Ground stations communicate with it during its passes, transmitting the new names that people submit through the website.
paragraph2: The more than 19,000 names sent before launch are in the satellite's memory, and everyone who sent one received a message when it ascended. New names join a queue and are transmitted by our ground station during the satellite's passes. You'll receive an email confirmation when yours has been uploaded to the Orbital Temple.
paragraph3: On January 12, 2026, the first satellite flew aboard ISRO's PSLV-C62. The rocket reached space but failed to deploy its payload. On Thursday, October 1, 2026, a second satellite launched on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission and reached orbit.
